question: A perfect square number can never have the digit ________ at the units’ place.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **units digit** of a **perfect square** is determined by the last digit of the number being squared.

Possible unit digits of 0 to 9 when squared are: 0, 1, 4, 9, 6, 5, 6, 9, 4, 1.

Therefore, a perfect square can only end in **0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9**.

It can **never** end in **2, 3, 7, or 8**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fda75b38188a016c9f502a4744fcc50f36533739a0c9f0862460dda8733b0519.png] 

**Given:** A set of natural numbers and their properties regarding **perfect squares**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1² = 1

⇒ 2² = 4

⇒ 3² = 9

⇒ 4² = 16 (unit digit 6)

⇒ 5² = 25 (unit digit 5)

⇒ 6² = 36 (unit digit 6)

⇒ 7² = 49 (unit digit 9)

⇒ 8² = 64 (unit digit 4)

⇒ 9² = 81 (unit digit 1)

⇒ 10² = 100 (unit digit 0)

⇒ Comparing the result set {0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9} with the given options, **8** is not present.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

A perfect square n² is always equal to the sum of the first n **consecutive odd numbers** (e.g., 4 = 1 + 3).

Digital Root Property

The **digital root** (sum of digits until a single digit is reached) of a perfect square can only be **1, 4, 7, or 9**.

Trailing Zeros

A perfect square always ends with an **even number of zeros** at the end of the number.</p
